turns.en: Your results have come back and I'm pleased to say everything looks normal. Your blood sugar was a little on the high side, so let's keep an eye on that.
turns.cy: Mae'ch canlyniadau chi wedi dod yn ôl, ac mae'n dda gen i ddeud bod bob dim yn edrych yn normal. Roedd eich siwgr gwaed chi braidd yn uchel, felly dewch i ni gadw golwg ar hynny.
chunks: Mae'ch canlyniadau chi wedi dod yn ôl
and I'm pleased to say everything looks normal
ac mae'n dda gen i ddeud bod bob dim yn edrych yn normal
pleasure relocates to mae'n dda gen i — the N-form fork; the bod that-clause under it
Your blood sugar was a little on the high side
Roedd eich siwgr gwaed chi braidd yn uchel
English's 'on the high side' hedge erases into braidd yn
so let's keep an eye on that
felly dewch i ni gadw golwg ar hynny
English's 'an eye' erases into the fixed cadw golwg
south: mae'n dda gyda fi — AND A REORDER
turns.southLine: Mae'ch canlyniadau chi wedi dod yn ôl, ac mae'n dda gyda fi weud bod popeth yn edrych yn normal. Roedd eich siwgr gwaed chi braidd yn uchel, felly dewch i ni gadw golwg ar hynny.

turns.en: Oh, thank goodness for that. What a relief.
turns.cy: O, diolch byth am hynny. Am ryddhad.
chunks: the fixed diolch byth; English's 'goodness' has no Welsh reflex
Welsh's exclamative takes am, not the interrogative word English uses

turns.en: It is good news. And the sugar is only just over the line - think of it as a nudge, well before any diagnosis.
turns.cy: Mae o'n newyddion da, ydy. Ac dim ond prin dros y llinell mae'r siwgr — meddyliwch amdano fo fel pwniad, ymhell cyn unrhyw ddiagnosis.
chunks: English marks the emphasis with a stressed auxiliary; Welsh appends the verb-echo ydy
And the sugar is only just over the line
Ac dim ond prin dros y llinell mae'r siwgr
the whole phrase fronts for focus, which English does with stress alone; 'only just' takes dim ond prin, not the erasing softener
think of it as a nudge, well before any diagnosis
meddyliwch amdano fo fel pwniad, ymhell cyn unrhyw ddiagnosis
meddwl governs am, conjugated as amdano fo

turns.en: At the doorstep. So I can still turn it round, can I?
turns.cy: Ar y trothwy. Felly mi fedra i ddal i'w droi o rownd, medra?
chunks: So I can still turn it round, can I?
Felly mi fedra i ddal i'w droi o rownd, medra?
the verb-echo tag medra — Welsh tags with the verb, and here the polarity stays positive

turns.en: You absolutely can - most people at this stage do. Cut the sugary drinks first, that's the biggest single win, and we'll re-test in three months.
turns.cy: Mi fedrwch, yn hollol — mae'r rhan fwya o bobl ar y cam yma yn gneud. Torrwch y diodydd melys gynta — dyna'r fuddugoliaeth fwya un — ac mi wnawn ni ail-brofi mewn tri mis.
chunks: the verb-echo answer; English's preverbal 'absolutely' lands after the verb in Welsh
most people at this stage do
mae'r rhan fwya o bobl ar y cam yma yn gneud
English's pro-verb 'do' has no Welsh reflex
English's attributive 'single' relocates to the postposed un; buddugoliaeth is feminine, so fwya
and we'll re-test in three months
ac mi wnawn ni ail-brofi mewn tri mis

turns.en: Three months. That's a fair challenge. I'll take it.
turns.cy: Tri mis. Mae hynna'n her deg. Mi gymra i hi.
chunks: feminine hi, agreeing with her — English's 'it' is genderless

turns.en: Everything looks normal, but your blood sugar was a little on the high side.
turns.cy: Mae bob dim yn edrych yn normal, ond roedd eich siwgr gwaed chi braidd yn uchel.
chunks: Mae bob dim yn edrych yn normal
but your blood sugar was a little on the high side
ond roedd eich siwgr gwaed chi braidd yn uchel

turns.en: High? How high? Should I be worried about that?
turns.cy: Uchel? Pa mor uchel? Ddylwn i boeni am hynny?
chunks: pa mor obligatory before the adjective
Should I be worried about that?
Welsh has no be-worried passive — poeni carries it

turns.en: It was 48. We like under 42, and diabetes starts at 48 - so you're right at the doorstep. Which makes this exactly the moment to act, while it's still easy.
turns.cy: Pedwar deg wyth oedd o. Dan ni'n licio o dan bedwar deg dau, ac mae diabetes yn dechra ar bedwar deg wyth — felly dach chi'n union ar y trothwy. Sy'n gneud hwn yn union yr adeg i weithredu, tra mae hi'n dal yn hawdd.
chunks: identificatory fronting; the number is read as a decimal (R5) and spelled out, so it reads aloud correctly
We like under 42, and diabetes starts at 48
Dan ni'n licio o dan bedwar deg dau, ac mae diabetes yn dechra ar bedwar deg wyth
so you're right at the doorstep
felly dach chi'n union ar y trothwy
English's intensifier 'right' relocates to yn union
Which makes this exactly the moment to act, while it's still easy
Sy'n gneud hwn yn union yr adeg i weithredu, tra mae hi'n dal yn hawdd
English's sentential 'which' becomes a bare sy'-relative; the tra clause-frame

turns.en: So I can still turn it round?
turns.cy: Felly mi fedra i ddal i'w droi o rownd?
chunks: So I can still turn it round?
Felly mi fedra i ddal i'w droi o rownd?
distinct from the tag version at F01-S04, which adds medra?

turns.en: Most people at this stage do. I'll get the nurse to book you into the lifestyle clinic - practical help, nobody's going to lecture you.
turns.cy: Mae'r rhan fwya o bobl ar y cam yma yn gneud. Mi wna i ofyn i'r nyrs eich bwcio chi i mewn i'r clinig ffordd o fyw — help ymarferol; does 'na neb yn mynd i bregethu wrthach chi.
chunks: Most people at this stage do
Mae'r rhan fwya o bobl ar y cam yma yn gneud
I'll get the nurse to book you into the lifestyle clinic
Mi wna i ofyn i'r nyrs eich bwcio chi i mewn i'r clinig ffordd o fyw
English's causative 'get X to' relocates to gofyn i — Welsh's gneud i would read as compulsion
practical help, nobody's going to lecture you
help ymarferol; does 'na neb yn mynd i bregethu wrthach chi
English's negative subject relocates to a negative existential; pregethu governs wrth

turns.en: No lectures - good. I get plenty of those at home.
turns.cy: Dim pregethu — da iawn. Dw i'n cael digon o'r rheiny adra.
chunks: English's plural noun becomes a Welsh verbal noun; there is no lecture-noun that reads here
I get plenty of those at home
Dw i'n cael digon o'r rheiny adra

turns.en: Everything looks normal, but your blood sugar was a little high - let's keep an eye on it.
turns.cy: Mae bob dim yn edrych yn normal, ond roedd eich siwgr gwaed chi braidd yn uchel — dewch i ni gadw golwg arno fo.
chunks: Mae bob dim yn edrych yn normal
but your blood sugar was a little high
ond roedd eich siwgr gwaed chi braidd yn uchel
converges with 'a little on the high side' — reception, welcome
let's keep an eye on it
dewch i ni gadw golwg arno fo

turns.en: Is that the diabetes coming, then? My mother had it, and her mother before her.
turns.cy: Ydy hynna'n golygu bod y diabetes yn dod, 'ta? Roedd o ar fy mam i, a'i mam hithau o'i blaen hi.
chunks: Is that the diabetes coming, then?
Ydy hynna'n golygu bod y diabetes yn dod, 'ta?
English's bare 'is that X coming' has no Welsh reflex — golygu bod, 'does that mean that', is what carries it
Roedd o ar fy mam i
an illness is ON a person in Welsh — ar, not the have-verb
a'i mam hithau o'i blaen hi
the conjunctive hithau, which English marks with stress alone

turns.en: Family history does raise the chances, you're right to mention it. But what you eat and how you move matters more - and small changes now make a real difference.
turns.cy: Mae hanes teulu yn codi'r siawns, ydy — dach chi'n iawn i sôn. Ond mae be dach chi'n ei fwyta a sut dach chi'n symud yn cyfri mwy — ac mae newidiadau bach rŵan yn gneud gwahaniaeth go iawn.
chunks: Family history does raise the chances
Mae hanes teulu yn codi'r siawns, ydy
English's emphatic 'does' becomes the appended verb-echo ydy
English's object 'it' erases — sôn is intransitive
But what you eat and how you move matters more
Ond mae be dach chi'n ei fwyta a sut dach chi'n symud yn cyfri mwy
two free relatives as a compound subject, each with its resumptive
and small changes now make a real difference
ac mae newidiadau bach rŵan yn gneud gwahaniaeth go iawn

turns.en: Small changes. My mother never got the chance to know early, see.
turns.cy: Newidiadau bach. Chafodd fy mam i erioed y cyfle i wybod yn gynnar, ylwch.
chunks: My mother never got the chance to know early
Chafodd fy mam i erioed y cyfle i wybod yn gynnar
the aspirate-mutated negative preterite carries English's 'never'; gwybod for factual knowing (S5)

turns.en: Then you've got the advantage she didn't. Cut the sugary drinks first, and we'll re-test in three months.
turns.cy: Mae gynnoch chi'r fantais na chafodd hi, 'ta. Torrwch y diodydd melys gynta, ac mi wnawn ni ail-brofi mewn tri mis.
chunks: Then you've got the advantage she didn't
Mae gynnoch chi'r fantais na chafodd hi, 'ta
the gan possessive; English's pro-verb 'didn't' becomes the full negative relative na chafodd
and we'll re-test in three months
ac mi wnawn ni ail-brofi mewn tri mis
south: mae … gyda chi — AND A REORDER
turns.southLine: Mae'r fantais na chafodd hi gyda chi, 'te. Torrwch y diodydd melys cynta', ac fe wnawn ni ail-brofi mewn tri mis.

turns.en: I'll take that challenge. For her, if nothing else.
turns.cy: Mi gymra i'r her yna. Er ei mwyn hi, os dim byd arall.
chunks: Er ei mwyn hi, os dim byd arall
benefactive 'for' is er mwyn in Welsh, not the plain preposition
